rejected.title: Indigenous rangers and protected areas
card: Indigenous ranger groups care for land and sea Country. Their work includes managing weeds and feral animals, monitoring wildlife and managing fire.
Rangers combine traditional knowledge, passed down over generations, with scientific methods. Each type of knowledge adds to the other.
An Indigenous Protected Area (IPA) is an area of land or sea that Indigenous people agree to manage for conservation. The owners choose to dedicate it, and it stays in their care.
IPAs make up a large part of Australia's conservation estate, the land and sea set aside to protect nature. Rangers often carry out the work on them.
rejected.remember: Rangers use traditional and scientific knowledge, and IPAs are Indigenous-managed land and sea that form a large part of Australia's conservation estate.

a.q: What is an Indigenous Protected Area?
opts: Land or sea that Indigenous people manage for conservation
A national park run only by a government agency
A farm that Indigenous people lease to mining companies
A reserve that the public is not allowed to enter
a.why: An IPA is dedicated by its Indigenous owners and managed by them to protect nature and culture. A national park run only by government is a different kind of protected area.
a.clue: Think about who decides how the area is managed.

b.q: A ranger group on the coast tracks turtle nests, using elders' knowledge of nesting times and scientists' tagging methods. What does this show?
opts: Traditional and scientific knowledge used together
Scientific knowledge replacing traditional knowledge
Traditional knowledge that scientists cannot use
Work that only governments are able to carry out
b.why: The rangers use elders' knowledge of nesting times alongside tagging methods from science. Neither replaces the other, so the work shows both kinds of knowledge combined.
b.clue: Count how many kinds of knowledge the rangers are using.

version.title: Indigenous rangers and protected areas
card: Indigenous ranger groups are teams of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people employed to care for land and sea Country. They control weeds and feral animals, manage fire and track wildlife.
Rangers combine traditional knowledge passed down from Elders with scientific tools such as drones, GPS tracking and data records. Each kind of knowledge adds to the other.
An Indigenous Protected Area (IPA) is land or sea that its Traditional Owners choose to dedicate to conservation, in an agreement with the Australian Government. It stays in their care.
IPAs make up about half the area of Australia's conservation estate, the network of land set aside to protect nature. Rangers do much of the work on them.
version.remember: Rangers bring two kinds of knowledge to their work, and IPAs protect a large share of Australia's nature.

a.q: Who decides that an area will become an Indigenous Protected Area?
opts: Its Traditional Owners, by choosing to dedicate it
A state government, by declaring a national park
A ranger group, by taking over land no one uses
Scientists, after finding rare species living there
a.why: An IPA is dedicated by its Traditional Owners, who agree with the Australian Government to manage it for conservation, and it stays in their care. A national park declared by a government is a different kind of protected area.
a.clue: Whose land or sea is it?

b.q: A ranger group uses Elders' knowledge of where feral pigs dig in a wetland, along with drone surveys, to plan where to set traps. What does this show?
opts: Traditional and scientific knowledge used together
Scientific methods taking the place of Elders' knowledge
Traditional knowledge that drones cannot add to
Pest control that needs no knowledge of the place
b.why: The rangers use what Elders know about the wetland alongside drone surveys from science. Neither replaces the other, so the plan uses both kinds of knowledge together.
b.clue: Count the kinds of knowledge the rangers use.

a.best: Its Traditional Owners, by choosing to dedicate it

b.best: Traditional and scientific knowledge used together
